content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation** (fails both preferred and fallback; borderline walk-away).

- **What we found:** Subparagraph 27.2 (p0263) affirmatively refuses to designate a governing law and directs all courts and tribunals to ignore the facts that would identify one; no other clause (Paragraph 25 compliance-with-law, Paragraph 20 privileges) selects a law, venue, or arbitral seat. Subparagraph 27.1 (p0262) makes Management Committee referral — which may itself impose arbitration — the "sole and exclusive remedy," leaving us with no court recourse.
- **Cure (preferred level, 2 operations):** Replace 27.2 with New York governing law plus exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County; conform 27.1 by removing the competing Committee-selected arbitration route and the "sole and exclusive remedy" bar, so the escalation step no longer defeats exclusive court jurisdiction. Fallback (Delaware/California, or England and Wales with the London courts) offered in the comment.
- Redline validated with `ok:true` and passed the minimality gate; unrelated text (reasonable-efforts escalation, continued performance) preserved verbatim.
